mark_price.description: D-85: current mark used for unrealised_usd. Absent/null means portfolio_metrics.py falls back to entry cost basis and flags the position as unmarked, never fabricates a price.

aqe_snapshot.description: D-85/D-91: AQE's market-data view of this held ticker (gics_sector, beta_30d, vol_30d_ann, sc_momentum, structure, elder, elder_5d, mp_accel_state, rs_leadership, flow, choch_state, bracket — see tools/held_book_refresh.py AQE_SNAPSHOT_FIELDS). Null until the loop has refreshed this position at least once; portfolio_metrics.py excludes null-snapshot positions rather than guessing. D-91: the first three keys were previously spelled sector/beta/ann_vol_pct — names no AQE export has ever carried — so they were dropped in silence on every refresh and sector_concentration was computed entirely against 'UNKNOWN'. Read any of these through held_book_refresh.snapshot_get, which resolves both spellings, rather than .get() on a bare key: journals written before the fix still carry the old shape.

aqe_snapshot_as_of.description: D-85: the date aqe_snapshot was actually refreshed (an AQE export date) — carried forward honestly by held_book_refresh.py carry-forward, so this is very often NOT today's date. Never silently reset.

aqe_snapshot_source.description: D-91: which block of the AQE export the snapshot was built from. AQE publishes a held name's record under daily_list only if it independently made the scored longlist — in the 25 Jul export that was 2 of 12 — and under held_positions for all of them. A 'held_positions' source means the snapshot is legitimately thinner (that block carries no elder_5d or rs_leadership); those fields are absent rather than null so a reader can tell 'not published' from 'looked up and empty'.

aegis_status.description: D-88: set by held_book_refresh.py classify_aegis_status, right after Operation 1 builds this row. 'confirmed' = matched a staged Aegis order (or already confirmed on a prior run). 'pending_review' = an unmatched broker fill, pulled in and risk-managed conservatively but EXCLUDED from portfolio_metrics.py's numbers until the PM confirms or rejects it at the next premarket approval. A fill matching the persistent non-Aegis exclusion list (data/persistent/non_aegis_exclusions.json) is never given a row at all — it is dropped before this field is ever set. null/absent is treated as confirmed, for rows written before this field existed.

occ_symbol.description: D-89: the 21-char OCC symbol as the broker spells it (ROOT + YYMMDD + C|P + strike in thousandths). Kept verbatim for audit; identity is NEVER taken from this string alone — see contract_key.

qty.description: D-89: SIGNED contracts — positive long, negative short. The sign is what distinguishes the two legs of a debit spread; an unsigned quantity makes the structure underivable.

greeks_as_of.description: D-89/D-90: timestamp of the Greeks/IV pull. Alpaca is the ONLY source serving Greeks at contract level and is 15-min delayed (Charter §0.5), so this is never 'now' — it is recorded so staleness stays visible rather than assumed. The Greek fields above are OPTIONAL and normally ABSENT at journal-write: post-market does not pull them (they are analytics, not book of record, and nothing in post-market reads them). Premarket's hedge-coverage assessment stamps them at the point of use, on the hedge legs only. Their absence is never a review flag — a flag firing on every journal ever written is flag fatigue.

contract_key.description: D-89: UNDERLYING|RIGHT|STRIKE(3dp)|EXPIRY — the canonical contract identity, written by tools/option_book.py. Strike normalised to 3 decimals so two brokers spelling 100 and 100.000 cannot look like two positions. Membership decisions key on THIS, never on ticker: SPY can host an Income Wheel put and an Aegis macro hedge at the same time.

structure_id.description: D-89: 'OPT:' + the sorted contract keys of the legs it belongs to. DERIVED, not assigned, so it is reproducible from a broker pull alone and leg order cannot produce two ids for one spread.

aegis_status.description: D-89: set by tools/option_book.py classify_option_status. 'confirmed' = the leg belongs to a structure the staging-gatekeeper actually staged, or its contract carries a recorded PM decision of 'aegis'. 'pending_review' = an unrecognised leg — KEPT and visible, flagged ONCE, but never fed to hedge derivation. A contract recorded 'not_aegis' in data/persistent/option_membership.json gets no row at all. The equity exclusion list (non_aegis_exclusions.json) is ticker-keyed and is NEVER consulted here.

role.description: D-89: 'hedge' for macro-hedge legs. Scope is hedge-only per PM ruling — income/wheel structures belong to other books and are not Aegis.

option_positions.description: D-89: option legs live HERE, never in open_positions — an option leg has a different identity (underlying+right+strike+expiry), a hard expiry lifecycle, and a different data source (Alpaca for Greeks) from an equity row. Legs are the truth; the hedge record below is DERIVED from them, so the structure can never quietly disagree with the broker.

dte.description: D-89: calendar days to expiry computed from journal.date, NOT the wall clock, so re-running an old journal reproduces the same number.

iv.description: D-89: mean leg IV. OMITTED ENTIRELY when the legs carry no IV — never present-and-null, because tools/calculators/hedge_engine.py reads hedge.get('iv', 0.20) and a null would break the coverage math where an absent key degrades to the documented default. The gap is flagged either way.

legs.description: contract keys of the confirmed legs this record was derived from

stale.description: D-89: true when the option book came back EMPTY while this record was on file. An empty broker pull and a genuinely closed hedge are indistinguishable from the data, so derive_hedge KEEPS the prior record marked stale and flags it HIGH rather than nulling it — a hedge must never vanish from the book because a call failed.

hedge.description: D-89: the CURRENT hedge structure, derived by tools/option_book.py derive_hedge from confirmed option_positions only — never hand-written, never carried forward blind. null means no confirmed hedge structure is held, honestly. Carries upper/lower/contracts/dte/iv (the fields hedge_engine.assess_current_hedge reads) PLUS the identity it previously lacked — underlying, expiry, and the legs it came from. Was an unconstrained stub with no writer anywhere in the kernel, which is why Phase 1 concluded 'no hedge on record' every morning while the book held one.

metrics.description: D-85/D-88: populated by tools/portfolio_metrics.py — gross_exposure_usd, leverage, net_beta_dollar, nav_beta, sector_concentration_pct, var, computed_from_aqe_dated, mixed_vintage, excluded_no_aqe_data, excluded_pending_review, missing_beta_or_vol, unmarked_cost_basis_proxy. Beta/ann_vol_pct are computed from FMP price history via tools/historical_store.py, not read from the AQE snapshot (D-88 — sector is the only AQE-sourced field left in this calc). No stop_audit key — that comparison is only ever fresh in premarket's own stop-update step, so it is not duplicated here. Lives HERE (not a separate file) so the journal is one proper portfolio snapshot, not just a list of positions (PM ruling, D-85). Recomputed unconditionally every run — deterministic and free, so there is no skip-if-unchanged logic.

review_flags.description: D-86: named, actionable exceptions any print-trade-journal operation finds — never blocks a write, always visible. Surfaced in the morning summary and the premarket held-book render, not buried in metrics.
